memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made fifty bronze clasps to fasten the tent together as a unit. Then they made for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of the other durable leather." - Exod 36:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four layers in total now. Fine linen inside. Goat hair over it. Ram skins dyed red. And on top, tough weatherproof leather.

God did not provide minimal protection for His dwelling place. He provided layer upon layer — beauty within, durability without, and everything in between.

That is a picture of how God guards what belongs to Him. Not one thin defence, but sustained, thorough care. Jesus said no one can snatch His sheep out of His hand, and no one can snatch them out of the Father's hand (John 10:28-29). Two hands. Layered security.

Notice that the outermost layer was the toughest and least beautiful. The part facing the desert wind took the punishment so the fine linen never had to.

Many of us have experienced God's protection this way without recognising it — a hardship absorbed, a door closed, a person who stood between us and something we never even saw coming.

We should also be careful not to promise more than Scripture does. God's protection does not mean believers are spared all suffering; the New Testament is honest about persecution and loss. But nothing reaches us that has not first passed through His hands, and nothing can separate us from His love in Christ (Rom 8:38-39).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has God protected you in ways you only recognised later?
2. Do you trust God's care even when hardship reaches you?
3. Who has God placed around you as a layer of protection?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for guarding what belongs to You. Help me trust Your care even when life is hard. Amen.
